title: ID 553: Introduction to the Principles of Instructional Design
description: A fully online, eight-module graduate-level introduction to instructional design. You will study the major ID models, analyze two realistic design cases, conduct learner and task analyses, write aligned objectives and assessments, plan and prototype an instructional intervention, and design its evaluation. The course follows the ADDIE arc (analysis, design, development, implementation, evaluation) while treating it critically, and every module produces a component of a final instructional plan you can carry into practice.
audience: Graduate students and practitioners new to instructional design: teachers, trainers, faculty developers, and technologists.
duration: Eight modules over 8 to 15 weeks. Plan on 6 to 8 hours per module.
instructor: Idowu David Awoyemi, The University of Alabama
